source: claude-code subagent (viewed all 3 contact sheets + profile + transcript)
summary: A two-part Ethiopia film that front-loads the most extreme imagery (Dallol's sulphur fields, Danakil salt miners and camel caravans) and then moves to its real subject, the walled city of Harar and its hand-fed hyenas. The opening 0:00-0:50 is a fast tease of both halves - acid-coloured terrain, Joe seated beside a hyena, a heat-struck presenter beside a 4x4 - over clipped narration. The Danakil section is shot in bright cyan-and-ochre daylight with strong process shots of salt extraction; Harar is a guided walk with a local, sit-down interviews and domestic interiors. The climax is a long night sequence of feeding hyenas under hard, warm practical light, ending with a walk into the dark toward the hyenas' 'home'. It closes on an Epidemic Sound sponsor read in an edit suite and a final camel-caravan sunset.
hook_analysis: Speech starts at 3 s ('The toxic gases... The smell...') over Dallol's colour fields (0:00-0:10). Within 30 s it cuts the night hyena-feeding image (0:20) and the presenter overwhelmed by heat (0:30), so both set-pieces are promised before any context. A second mini-hook at 0:40-0:50 states the hyena premise directly. The 0:00-0:12 replay peak confirms the colour-field opening as the strongest grab.
narrative_arc: No chapters. Tease (0:00-1:07) -> Danakil salt-miners history with archival-style rock art and maps (1:07-2:29) -> on-the-ground salt mining and Dallol volcano (2:29-5:37) -> travel to Harar via airport, markets and map (5:47-7:26) -> guided walk through old city, kite-feeding, traditional house (7:26-12:32) -> expert interview framing the hyena question (12:42-13:42) -> dusk then night hyena feeding with the Hyena Man (13:52-19:08) -> walk into darkness (19:18-20:38) -> sponsor and caravan sunset (20:47-21:37).
camera_and_composition: Low-angle hero framing of workers against flat cyan sky (2:58, 3:48); top-down drone showing a single figure in a salt hole (5:27-5:37) for scale; locked two-shot seated interviews repeated across many tiles (12:52-13:42, 16:30-17:00) - a static, studio-like setup in a garden and at night; wide-angle selfie in heat (2:38). Night feeding is lit with a warm practical/red-orange source low in frame. Camera moves are not observable at storyboard resolution.
color_and_grade: Highly saturated with cyan skies and teal-pushed whites (Harar's walls read mint/teal, 7:55-9:05) against ochre/red sulphur and earth. Night section shifts to deep blue ambient with warm orange key on faces; the hotel interior at 20:28 is lurid green. Archival hyena close-up at 17:20 has a different, warmer natural-history look.
sound_and_music: Speech-heavy (60% coverage, ~127 wpm) with short speech-free runs (max ~27 s) e.g. 2:00-2:26 caravan, 5:46-6:00 travel, 13:48-14:06 hyena reveal. 53 questions in the transcript - Joe drives scenes by asking locals questions. The sponsor read says most music and ambience came from Epidemic Sound and admits ambient sound sometimes isn't recorded on location.
what_to_borrow: Tease both halves of a two-location film in the first 30 s, ending on the most unusual image
Use a top-down drone with one tiny human figure to sell the scale of a harsh landscape
Before the spectacle, insert an expert sit-down that frames the question so the set-piece answers it
Let the night set-piece play as a continuous escalating sequence rather than intercutting it
what_to_avoid_copying: Cutting third-party broadcast footage (a BBC-badged hyena close-up at 17:20) into your own film without rights
Repeating the same static two-shot for 50+ seconds of interview - it is visibly unvaried across tiles
Placing a long sponsor read right after the climax
